name: Keep Solitary
specific_features: A perfectly cuboid boulder, 12m per side, resting on the mesa summit with no explanation for its geometry
description: Keep Solitary is a small, airless world orbiting alone in the outer reaches of a sparse system, its surface a featureless expanse of smooth basalt interrupted by a single enormous mesa that rises three kilometers above the surrounding plains. The mesa's flat summit and near-vertical walls give it the unmistakable profile of a keep or tower, standing sentinel over nothing. Regolith dust drifts collect against its base in grey banks.

The loneliness of Keep Solitary is palpable even through a viewport. No other bodies orbit nearby, no moons attend it, and the system's star is a dim point providing just enough light to see by. The silence is total, and the stillness absolute -- nothing has moved on this world under its own power for as long as geological time can measure. It is a monument to emptiness.

On the mesa's summit sits an object that defies easy explanation: a perfectly cuboid boulder, twelve meters on each side, composed of the same basalt as the mesa itself but with machined-precise geometry that cannot be attributed to natural processes. No tool marks, no seams, no joints -- just twelve-meter faces of flawless stone. It has been there long enough for micrometeorite impacts to dust its surface but not long enough, apparently, to significantly erode its edges.

Keep Solitary attracts a particular kind of visitor: those drawn to mysteries that resist resolution. The cube has been scanned, sampled, and debated across academic journals without consensus. Some call it a natural formation of extraordinary improbability; others insist it is artificial but cannot explain who placed it or why. The planet offers no other clues, no other anomalies -- just the cube, the mesa, and the silence.
